# DigiKey.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/digikey-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/digikey-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects product and listing data from DigiKey.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape DigiKey Pricing, Stock, and Specs in 2026](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-digikey)
- **Code:** [`digikey.py`](digikey.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Category](results/category.json) · [Products](results/products.json) · [Search](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- DigiKey product pages for product data, pricing, stock, specifications and compliance info
- DigiKey category/filter pages for product listing data
- DigiKey keyword search pages for listing data

## Functions

- `scrape_products(urls)` → `List[DigikeyProduct]`
- `scrape_category(url, max_pages=3)` → `List[DigikeyCategoryResult]`
- `scrape_search(keywords)` → `List[DigikeyKeywordResult]`

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import digikey


async def main():
    category = await digikey.scrape_category(
        url="https://www.digikey.com/en/products/filter/industrial-automation-accessories/800",
        max_pages=3,
    )
    search = await digikey.scrape_search(keywords="Power Transformers")


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`DigikeyProduct`**: `name`, `url`, `digikey_part_number`, `manufacturer_part_number?`, `manufacturer?`, `description?`, `category?`, `price?`, `currency?`, `price_breaks?`, `stock_quantity?`, `availability?`, `lead_time?`, `min_order_qty?`, `lifecycle_status?`, `rohs_status?`, `reach_status?`, `msl_rating?`, `datasheet_url?`, `image?`, `specifications`
- **`DigikeyCategoryResult`**: `name?`, `url?`, `digikey_part_number?`, `manufacturer_part_number?`, `manufacturer?`, `price?`, `currency?`, `stock_quantity?`, `availability?`, `image?`
- **`DigikeyKeywordResult`**: `name`, `url`, `manufacturer`, `manufacturer_part_number`, `price`, `currency`, `stock_quantity`, `image`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`digikey.py`](digikey.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser
- `country` = `"us"`: country of the proxy

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/digikey-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_product_scraping`, `test_category_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
